@minormobius.bsky.social: Reasonable start. I think the interlocking is critical, you should make a geometric model and run the fish as tesselating polygons. Then the Poincaré conformal map will be sensible, and the interlocking falls out ~for free

@minormobius.bsky.social: Yes but. They have to look like fish! And they have to extend endlessly. So you’re always generating some radius around center with a mathematical description of the tiling. As long as you keep the geometry periodic it’s gonna be fiiine. I know drawing is a challenge so why dont you do hex tiling

@minormobius.bsky.social: Still not infinite. It HAS to be infinite tilings

@minormobius.bsky.social: Rebuilding the patch is the right idea. Currently the patch doesn’t extend out so eg you scroll far enough over and just get patches of one rebuilt. Secondly it’s not smooth. It’s gotta be smooth, no jerky jerky. You might be better served by building a buffer, and retiring tiles exceeding threshold
